answer.text:
The weekly status reports support only a narrow claim: the nightly article extract job ran and its file landed without reported errors. Ana Duarte's weekly updates list "Nightly article extract completed, no errors" as a topic worked on in the updates of 12 January 2026 (R01M004), 9 February 2026 (R01M003) and 9 March 2026 (R01M002). At the Q2 business review on 16 June 2026, when Ana Duarte noted "The weeklies said the extract completed" (T22U0136), Nadia Haddad confirmed: "They did. It did. The job ran and the file landed every night. That is what completed means in that line. Nobody has ever checked what was in it." (T22U0137, T22U0138, T22U0139). So the reports are evidence of job execution status only. [1] [2] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7]

The reports are not evidence that the extract contents were correct or ever checked. Nadia Haddad stated at the Q2 review that she had compared the extract totals against till numbers for January to March and "They do not reconcile. The extract is lower." (T22U0130, T22U0132), adding that it is "not a rounding difference" (T22U0135) while declining to give a number she had held for only two days (T22U0134, T22U0135). As of 16 June 2026 no cause had been identified: "Understood. I do not have a cause yet." (T22U0146). [8] [9] [10] [11] [12]

The discrepancy matters for reported figures because the Q1 waste numbers were derived from the extract. Nadia Haddad's April 2026 note stated "The tonnage is derived from the article movement totals in the nightly extract, not counted from till data" (E10M004), and at the Q2 review she confirmed the 3.4% figure "Is derived off those totals, yes" (T22U0140, T22U0141). The Q1 reporting email gave fresh waste of 3.4% against a 4.1% baseline and an absolute reduction of approximately 118 tonnes over the quarter (E10M004); Lena Fischer's summary of "3.4 percent. Target is 2.8" (E10M003) and Ana Duarte's weekly of 6 April 2026 citing "Q1 fresh waste 3.4% against a 4.1% baseline" (R01M001) rest on that same extract-derived basis. [13] [14] [15] [16] [17]

Silent success is a known failure mode on this project. In the April 2024 technical due diligence, Priya Nair described silent failure as "the job reports success and moves nothing. We find out when somebody notices the numbers are yesterday's." (T02U0076), and the 9 February 2026 weekly separately flagged that the "DC-2 feed failed twice in January. Less often than before go-live but still failing." (R01M003). This is why "completed, no errors" in the weeklies has never been a sufficient check on its own. [18] [2]

Evidence gap: the archive contains no extract-level validation or reconciliation records for the January to March 2026 period itself. The only direct evidence about extract content quality is Nadia Haddad's reconciliation finding reported on 16 June 2026, and its cause was still unknown at that date.

Recommendation: treat "completed, no errors" in the weekly updates as a job-execution status only, and require a reconciliation of extract totals against till data as a standing check before any further board reporting of extract-derived figures. This follows from the observed pattern that the weeklies reported successful completion while the extract did not reconcile with till data (T22U0132), the Q1 board figures were derived from those totals (E10M004, T22U0141), and silent success was flagged as a known risk as early as the 2024 due diligence (T02U0076). [9] [13] [15] [18]

citations.quote:
Hello,

First full quarter of fresh live. Numbers against the baseline we agreed in December.

Produce and dairy, 25 pilot stores, January to March:

  Fresh waste            4.1% -> 3.4% of fresh net sales
  Absolute reduction     approximately 118 tonnes over the quarter
  Estimated CO2e avoided approximately 296 tonnes
  Availability           +1.9 points
  Order automation       88% on the categories in scope

The CO2e figure uses the conversion factors in your own sustainability report rather
than ours, so it should reconcile with what you publish.

Chilled ready meals is not in these numbers, it went live too late in the quarter.

Two caveats. The baseline quarter had an unusually warm February which flatters produce.
And the 118 tonnes is scaled from 25 stores, so please do not multiply it up to the full
estate in any external communication without talking to us first.

One note on how it is arrived at. The tonnage is derived from the article movement totals
in the nightly extract, not counted from till data. That is the normal basis and it has
been stable all quarter, but it is a derivation rather than a count and I would rather say
so than have it come up later.

Nadia Haddad

answer.question: The weekly status reports say the nightly article extract completed with no errors. Is that true? Answer the question the reports are actually evidence for, and say what they are not evidence for.
trace: Read 2974 permitted source records at L3.
Checked all three weekly updates for the exact 'Nightly article extract completed, no errors' line and dates (R01M004 12 Jan, R01M003 9 Feb, R01M002 9 Mar 2026)

Confirmed the Q2 review exchange: Ana Duarte's 'The weeklies said the extract completed' (T22U0136) and Nadia Haddad's confirmation across T22U0137-T22U0139, including the fragmented sentence completed in T22U0139
Verified the non-reconciliation claim is supported by T22U0130 and T22U0132, with 'not a rounding difference' in T22U0135 and no number given (T22U0134-T22U0135)
Verified 'no cause yet' attribution to Nadia Haddad in T22U0146
Verified 3.4%, 4.1% baseline and ~118 tonnes appear in E10M004; 3.4% also in E10M003 and R01M001; derivation-from-extract stated in E10M004 and confirmed in T22U0140-T22U0141
Verified 18 quoted passages against runtime sources.
